project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description:
_Please provide highly descriptive information for each field_

||*Field*||*Value*||
|Source Object (DB/Schema/Table)| |
|Bronze Table Name| |
|Business Description| |
|Row Identifier / Natural Key / Uniqueness| |
|Delta Column (if any)| |
|Deletion Handling| |
|Refresh Cadence| |

h3. Acceptance Criteria

comments:
Ticket REQ0168685 raised with EUC team. Screenshot and session ID provided for access failure. Neville has responded and would revert back on {{2026-02-10}}.

Had a troubleshoot session with Neville. We found out the there is some settings in the storage account network that further restricts logging in from the jumpbox’s private endpoint.

Neville helped to install MS Storage Explorer in the jumpbox but still faced the same issue.

We need to reach out to cloud team to investigate and resolve this

Would need to note down this with [https://sigmahealthcare.atlassian.net/browse/CSCI-811|https://sigmahealthcare.atlassian.net/browse/CSCI-811] and raise as issues in project meeting so Oded can follow up on his end as well - @user to action

After discussing the storage account setup with Eugene, we identified that DNS integration and the necessary firewall configuration between the storage account and the jumpbox were not in place, which explains the current access issue. This gives us a clear starting point for the investigation.

I’ve shared this information with Neville, and he will come back to me tomorrow with next steps.

It is being blocked. Pending support from the Cloud team. @user

h3. Context

* The Azure Pipelines implementation follows a shared, parameterized design pattern. Pipeline behaviour is dynamically determined at runtime through configurable parameters, allowing data loads to be executed for multiple tables using a single pipeline definition.
At present, all data is being loaded into the {{EDP_DEV_LEGACY}} environment.

h3. Objective

* The proposed design introduces a clear separation of pipeline responsibilities by dividing them into two categories:
** Tactical solutions, which will handle data refreshes within the {{EDP_DEV_LEGACY}} environment.
*** Jess’s PBI work
*** NLP Solution
*** APPRISS
** Strategic EDP pipelines, which will manage data refreshes within the {{EDP}} environment.
* This approach preserves the integrity of the {{EDP_DEV}} environment by isolating it from tactical or short-term solutions.

h3. Steps 

# Create a clean folder structure.
# New linked service of EDP_DEV_LEGACY
# Test the data is flowing as expected.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Complete isolation of EDP environment from tactical solutions. 

h3.

h3. 

h3.

comments:
Below is the root cause summary:

 

The Microsoft Entra ID SCIM integration runs fully in the cloud and outside our subscription/VNet, so it cannot access the Snowflake PrivateLink endpoint. Since we disabled Snowflake’s public endpoint in December, the SCIM provisioning logs show “succeeded,” but no new users are created. This is a typically quiet process in AAD, so errors are not actively surfaced. The cloud team member, Raveen K, who helped us provision Snowflake SCIM has since resigned, so I suspect any error message from the Microsoft Entra ID side was never communicated to us.

I will run through the solution options with Alan and Mike first. I will reach out to Hallmark Santuyo once have the confirmed position.

o resolve this, we have two options:

Option 1: Open the required access in our network policy so only SCIM can reach Snowflake over a public route. All other data access still go through private endpoints. This can be tightly controlled via network rules.

 

Option 2: Use a SCIM provisioning local agent deployed inside our VNet to handle provisioning traffic internally.

@user @user @user 

Mike has confirmed to go with Option 1.

Hi all, I've set up the new network policies for us but Entra SCIM provisioning is still not fully functional. I applied a temporary fix so Tanya and Eugene can access Snowflake via SSO. It appears the MS Entra network setup is more complex than I initially expected. I'll keep working with Brent and the team to resolve this next week.@user @user

Issues to resolve: 

* Connection Entra - Snowflake after the new network policy
* Auto-provisioning (users and groups assigning)

I’ve emailed Brent to advise one which IP range I can use for SCIM

Reached out to Brent for NAT Outbound range confirmation. Awaiting feedback.

Had to cancel my meeting with Brent due to other priority from his side. Will rebook a meeting at some stage next week.

Followed up with Brent today. He mentioned to catch up later this week to discuss the resolution.

SNOW RITM0185270

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
summary: SC Tactical Reporting || SC Warehouse Creation
description:
h2. Overview

Create a *dedicated Snowflake warehouse* to support *SC Tactical Reporting* workloads. This warehouse will be isolated from other analytics workloads to ensure predictable performance, cost control, and clear ownership. A defined quota and usage limits will be applied to prevent resource contention and unplanned cost growth.

h2. Steps

# Define requirements for the SC Tactical Reporting warehouse, including size, auto-suspend/resume settings, and concurrency needs.
# Create a new dedicated Snowflake warehouse for SC Tactical Reporting.
# Configure warehouse parameters (auto-suspend, auto-resume, scaling policy, timeout).
# Apply warehouse-level quota / resource monitor to control credit consumption.
# Assign appropriate roles and grants to allow SC Tactical Reporting users and services to access the warehouse.
# Validate workload isolation by confirming SC Tactical queries are running exclusively on the new warehouse.
# Document the warehouse configuration, quota limits, and usage guidelines.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A dedicated Snowflake warehouse for SC Tactical Reporting is created and available.
* Warehouse configuration aligns with agreed performance and cost requirements.
* A quota or resource monitor is applied and actively enforcing limits.
* Required roles/users can access the warehouse, with no unnecessary permissions.
* SC Tactical Reporting queries run successfully using the new warehouse.
* Configuration and usage guidelines are documented and shared with stakeholders.

summary: Config IP restrictions in dbt Cloud
description:
h3. Context

As part of the "DBT Implementation" project, there is a requirement to enhance the security of dbt Cloud by configuring IP restrictions. Implementing IP allowlists ensures that only users and systems connecting from approved network locations can access dbt Cloud resources. This measure helps protect sensitive data and reduces the risk of unauthorized access by limiting entry points to trusted IP addresses, in line with organizational security policies.

Reference: [Configuring IP restrictions | dbt Developer Hub|https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/cloud/secure/ip-restrictions]

h3. Acceptance Criteria 

# Define the SaaS applications/cloud whose IP will be whitelisted. This would include:
## Snowflake - all accounts (CW, Sigma, Ireland)
## Azure tenancy (CW, Sigma, Ireland)
## Entra ID (for authentication)
## Azure DevOps
# IP allowlist/restriction settings are configured in dbt Cloud to permit access only from approved IP addresses or ranges.
# The configuration is documented, including:
#* The list of allowed IP addresses/ranges.
#* Steps for updating or maintaining the allowlist.
# A successful test is performed to verify that only connections from allowed IPs can access dbt Cloud, and unauthorized IPs are blocked.
# The configuration aligns with organizational security and compliance requirements.
# The setup is reviewed and approved by relevant stakeholders (e.g., Security or IT team)

summary: F03: Milestone 3 – CI/CD, IaC, Observability & Medallion Patterns
description:
*Milestone 3 – CI/CD, IaC, Observability & Medallion Patterns (Silver to Platinum to Gold)*

* CI/CD pipelines and IaC patterns in place and successfully promoting changes between environments.
* IaC patterns in place for key Snowflake/dbt configuration
* Observability and data quality tooling integrated with dbt Cloud, with dashboards available to Sigma Healthcare
* Standard patterns and templates documented and implemented in dbt for: Bronze to Silver, Silver to Platinum, Platinum to Gold.
* Reference implementation: A narrow end to end example (eg.1 x simple dimension) built from Bronze to Silver to Platinum to Gold using the agreed patterns to prove design and serve as a working template.
* Data engineers enabled to independently start building Bronze to Silver transformations using dbt.

summary: Setup Terraform for dbt Cloud Setup
description:
h3. Context

As part of the "DBT Implementation" project, there is a need to automate and standardize the infrastructure provisioning for dbt Cloud environments. Setting up Terraform will enable Infrastructure as Code (IaC) practices, allowing for consistent, repeatable, and auditable deployment of dbt Cloud resources. This task involves creating and configuring Terraform scripts/modules to manage dbt Cloud setup, ensuring alignment with organizational standards and best practices.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

# Terraform scripts/modules are created to provision and configure dbt Cloud resources as required for the project.
# The Terraform code is stored in the designated version-controlled repository (Azure DevOps).
# All required variables, secrets, and configurations are parameterized and securely managed (e.g., using environment variables or secret stores).
# Documentation is provided, detailing:
#* How to initialize, plan, and apply the Terraform configuration.
#* Any prerequisites or dependencies.
#* Rollback or destroy procedures.
# A successful test run is performed, demonstrating that the Terraform scripts can provision the necessary dbt Cloud resources without errors.
# The setup is reviewed and approved by relevant stakeholders (e.g., DevOps or Cloud Engineering team).
# No sensitive information (such as secrets or credentials) is hardcoded or exposed in the Terraform code or documentation.

summary: Generate key pair values for service user account - Sigma Snowflake Account
description:
*Context*

As part of the "DBT Implementation" project, there is a requirement to securely enable service user access to the Sigma Snowflake Account. To facilitate secure authentication and automation, a key pair (public and private keys) must be generated for the designated service user account. This will allow the service user to connect to Snowflake using key pair authentication, which is a best practice for enhanced security and automation.

Reference: [Key-pair authentication and key-pair rotation | Snowflake Documentation|https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/key-pair-auth]

*Acceptance Criteria*

# A new key pair (public and private keys) is generated specifically for the service user account intended for the Sigma Snowflake Account.
# The private key is securely stored and shared only with authorized personnel, following organizational security policies.
# The public key is provided and configured in the Sigma Snowflake Account for the service user.
# Private key is stored in Azure Key Vault for future reference 
# Verification is performed to ensure the service user can successfully authenticate from dbt Cloud to Snowflake using the generated key pair.
# No sensitive key material is exposed in Jira or any unsecured location.

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
summary: Create Snowflake local user account for dbt Cloud connection - Sigma Snowflake
description:
h3. *Context*

dbt Cloud requires a dedicated user account in the Sigma Snowflake environment to establish a secure and auditable connection. The user is of type “Service”. Creating a local Snowflake user account specifically for dbt Cloud ensures that data transformations and operations performed by dbt Cloud are properly attributed, access is controlled, and security best practices are followed. This setup is essential for maintaining compliance, monitoring activity, and managing permissions effectively within the Snowflake environment.

Refer to following for details: [Create a secure service account in Snowflake · GitHub|https://gist.github.com/apd-bbaker/9753e1422818028c0bccc99955ecef2a], [CREATE USER | Snowflake Documentation|https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/create-user]

h3. Acceptance Criteria

# *Snowflake User Account Created*
#* A new local user account is created in the Sigma Snowflake environment specifically for dbt Cloud integration.
#* The username follows the agreed naming convention (e.g., dbt_cloud_cw).
# *Appropriate Roles and Permissions Assigned*
#* The user account is granted only the necessary roles and permissions required for dbt Cloud operations.
#* Permissions are reviewed to ensure least privilege is applied.

description:
h3. Context

As part of the "DBT Implementation" project, there is a requirement to configure SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) provisioning from Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory). This integration will automate the user and group provisioning process, ensuring that user access to the relevant systems is managed efficiently and securely. By enabling SCIM, user lifecycle management (creation, updates, deactivation) will be synchronized between Entra ID and the target application, reducing manual effort and improving compliance.

Reference: [Set up SCIM | dbt Developer Hub|https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/cloud/manage-access/scim#assign-users-to-scim-app], [Set up SCIM | dbt Developer Hub|https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/cloud/manage-access/scim#manage-user-licenses-with-scim]

# User and group provisioning (creation, updates, and deactivation) is automated and synchronized between Entra ID and the target system.
# User license assignments are done via SCIM.
# The configuration follows organizational security and compliance standards.
# A successful test is performed to verify that user and group changes in Entra ID are reflected in dbt Cloud.
# The setup is reviewed and approved by relevant stakeholders (e.g., IT Security or Identity Management team).

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description:
h2. Overview

This card outlines the work required to generate an Appriss benchmark data scenario. Generating this data will allow us to accurately benchmark the performance of our systems against a realistic dataset, ensuring optimal performance and scalability. This benchmark data will be used to identify potential bottlenecks and optimize system configurations.

h2. Steps

# Identify the key data elements required for the Appriss benchmark scenario based on existing system usage patterns.
# Develop a data generation script or tool capable of creating synthetic data that mimics the characteristics of real Appriss data, including volume, distribution, and relationships between data elements.
# Configure the data generation tool to produce a dataset of sufficient size to accurately represent a realistic Appriss workload.
# Execute the data generation script to create the benchmark dataset.
# Validate the generated data to ensure it accurately reflects the characteristics of real Appriss data and meets the defined requirements.
# Document the data generation process, including the configuration parameters and validation results.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* All appliable scenario has been identified and transaction id shared to Business to regenerate receipt

* [ ] Any escalated issues have been assigned to the appropriate team.

description:
h2. Overview

This card outlines the work required to establish RF tactical access. Providing RF tactical access will enable secure and reliable communication in environments where traditional network infrastructure is unavailable. This is crucial for maintaining operational effectiveness and situational awareness in critical scenarios.

h2. Steps

# Define the specific requirements for RF tactical access, including frequency bands, data rates, and security protocols.
# Identify and procure the necessary hardware and software components, such as radios, antennas, and encryption modules.
# Configure and integrate the RF equipment to establish a functional tactical network.
# Conduct thorough testing of the RF tactical access solution to ensure performance and reliability under various conditions.
# Develop comprehensive documentation and training materials for users of the RF tactical access system.
# Deploy the RF tactical access solution in the designated operational environment.
# Provide ongoing support and maintenance for the RF tactical access system.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] The RF tactical access solution meets the defined requirements for frequency bands, data rates, and security protocols.
* [ ] The RF equipment is properly configured and integrated, allowing for seamless communication.
* [ ] The RF tactical access solution demonstrates reliable performance under simulated operational conditions.
* [ ] Comprehensive documentation and training materials are available for users.
* [ ] The RF tactical access solution is successfully deployed in the designated operational environment.
* [ ] A support and maintenance plan is in place for the RF tactical access system.

Hi @user, could you please run your eyes over this?

Have also added a DDL in the STTM document, as well as “baseline logic” to help populate the Dim:

DDL

{code:sql}CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE DIM_TIME (
 TimeKey INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 1..86400
 TimeValue24Hour STRING(8) NOT NULL, -- HH:MM:SS
 TimeValue12Hour STRING(11) NOT NULL, -- 3:23:11 PM
 Hour24Hour INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 0..23
 Hour12Hour INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 1..12
 Minute INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 0..59
 Second INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 0..59
 AMPM STRING(2) NOT NULL, -- AM / PM
 SecondOfHour INTEGER NOT NULL, -- Minute*60 + Second
 SecondsSinceMidnight INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 0..86399
 HourMinute24Hour STRING(5) NOT NULL, -- HH:MM
 HourMinute12Hour STRING(8) NOT NULL, -- 3:23 PM
 HourlyInterval24Hour STRING(11) NOT NULL, -- 01:00-02:00
 HourlyInterval12Hour STRING(17) NOT NULL, -- 01:00 AM-02:00 AM
 TimeOfDay STRING(10) NOT NULL -- Morning/Afternoon/Evening/Night
)
COMMENT = 'Time dimension at 1-second grain (86,400 rows per day)'
;{code}

_Baseline Logic*_

{code:sql}WITH Seconds AS (
 SELECT TOP (86400)
 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) - 1 AS s
 FROM sys.all_objects
)
INSERT INTO DimTime
SELECT
 s + 1 AS TimeKey,
 CONVERT(CHAR(8), DATEADD(SECOND, s, '00:00:00'), 108) AS TimeValue,
 s / 3600 AS Hour,
 (s % 3600) / 60 AS Minute,
 s % 60 AS Second,
 s AS SecondsSinceMidnight,

 CASE WHEN (s / 3600) % 12 = 0 THEN 12 ELSE (s / 3600) % 12 END AS Hour12,
 CASE WHEN s / 3600 < 12 THEN 'AM' ELSE 'PM' END AS AMPM,

 s / 3600 AS HourKey,
 s / 60 AS MinuteKey,
 s % 3600 AS SecondOfHour,

 FORMAT(DATEADD(SECOND, s, '00:00:00'), 'h:mm:ss tt') AS TimeLabel,

 CASE
 WHEN s / 3600 BETWEEN 6 AND 11 THEN 'Morning'
 WHEN s / 3600 BETWEEN 12 AND 17 THEN 'Afternoon'
 WHEN s / 3600 BETWEEN 18 AND 21 THEN 'Evening'
 ELSE 'Night'
 END AS TimeOfDay,

 CASE WHEN s / 3600 BETWEEN 6 AND 11 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
 CASE WHEN s / 3600 BETWEEN 12 AND 17 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
 CASE WHEN s / 3600 BETWEEN 18 AND 21 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
 CASE WHEN s / 3600 NOT BETWEEN 6 AND 21 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,

 s / 1800 AS HalfHourBucket,
 s / 900 AS QuarterHourBucket,
 s / 300 AS FiveMinuteBucket,

 CASE WHEN s % 3600 = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END,
 CASE WHEN s % 60 = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description:
h2. Overview

Snowflake has advised that our current multi-account setup should be restructured under a single *Sigma Healthcare Snowflake Organization* to fully enable capabilities such as Internal Marketplace data sharing (particularly between Ireland and Sigma Aus). Today, Sigma and CW exist under separate Snowflake organizations, which prevents us from leveraging these platform features. This card captures the assessment and remediation work required to fix the Snowflake Organization setup.

h2. Steps

# Review current Snowflake Organization configuration across Sigma and CW accounts.
# Document gaps between current setup and recommended structure (Sigma Healthcare Org CW, Ireland, Sigma Aus, Middle East).
# Engage Snowflake Support/Solutions Architect to confirm migration options, prerequisites, and risks.
# Assess impacts on billing, RBAC, account-level objects, integrations, PrivateLink, and network policies.
# Define a proposed transition plan with required sequencing for organization consolidation.
# Present findings and recommendations to the EDP platform team and stakeholders for approval.
# Execute agreed migration tasks (if approved) and validate post-migration functionality—especially Internal Marketplace sharing between Ireland and Sigma Aus.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Current Snowflake org structure is documented and validated.
* Gap analysis completed outlining impacts and required changes.
* Recommendations endorsed by Snowflake and internal platform leads.

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description:
h2. Overview

The existing Appriss Datashare ELT query requires refinement to improve accuracy, maintainability, and alignment with the current data product standards. This work ensures the ELT logic is consistent with the latest Appriss data-share requirements, resolves gaps identified during QA, and prepares the pipeline for downstream reporting dependencies.

h2. Steps

# Review the current Appriss Datashare ELT SQL and document all existing joins, filters, transformations, and business rules.
# Identify inconsistencies, redundant logic, missing filters, or misaligned business definitions based on updated Appriss documentation and stakeholder feedback.
# Update and refine the SQL ELT logic to reflect the correct business rules, ensuring alignment with Bronze → Silver conventions and naming standards.
# Validate refined output against expected Appriss samples (e.g., benchmark extracts, QA logs, historical outputs).
# Optimise query performance where appropriate (index use, partition pruning, CTE structure, join ordering).
# Peer review with Data Engineering and validate with Appriss SME before promoting the updated query.
# Update documentation, lineage, and add comments within the SQL code for ongoing maintainability.

h2. Deliverables

* Refined and validated Appriss Datashare ELT SQL query.
* Comparison document outlining logic changes vs previous version.
* Updated data lineage / documentation in Confluence & Alation.
* Peer-review sign-off and test results.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* All business rules in the refined ELT logic align with current Appriss data share specifications.
* Output datasets match expected Appriss benchmarks with no material discrepancies.
* SQL code passes peer review and conforms to internal coding standards.
* Performance is equal to or better than the existing ELT job.
* Documentation and lineage links are updated and published.

* [ ] The Supply Chain team has the necessary permissions to access the Datashare and the designated warehouse.

{code:sql}CASE
 WHEN l.PROFILE_ID = 'QLD1' THEN
 CASE
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 101 AND 118 THEN 'CLS'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 119 AND 128 THEN 'TC'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 301 AND 306 THEN 'Cage'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 501 AND 502 THEN 'Bulk'
 ELSE NULL
 END
 WHEN l.PROFILE_ID = 'SOM' THEN
 CASE
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 104 AND 125 THEN 'General CLS'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 401 AND 403 THEN 'Ethical CLS'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 301 AND 314 THEN 'Cage CLS'
 ELSE NULL
 END
 WHEN l.PROFILE_ID = 'NSW1' THEN
 CASE
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 101 AND 128 THEN 'CLS Zone'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 301 AND 311 THEN 'Cage DG'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) = 312 THEN 'Cage General'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) = 181 THEN 'TC General'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) = 402 THEN 'TC Ethical'
 WHEN CAST(l.ZONE_PICKING_ZONE_ID AS UNSIGNED) BETWEEN 501 AND 502 THEN 'Bulk'
 ELSE NULL
 END
 ELSE NULL
 END{code}

description:

* Create modular and reusable IaC templates for these objects.
* Ensure templates follow organisational standards for naming, security, and compliance.

Lower level objects to be scripted:

* Resource Monitors

will be addressed and refined in subsequent iterations.

To confirm inputs from Alan and Mike on the below:

We currently have service users for ADF (S_ADF_DEV) and PowerBI (S_POWERBI_DEV) following the Sigma Snowflake account convention.
Should these be renamed to align with the naming convention outlined in the [Snowflake Security Overview|https://sigmahealthcare.atlassian.net/wiki/x/AQBDY] ?
If yes, I’ll coordinate with Mike on naming and work with Ashu/Jess to update ADF and PowerBI configurations accordingly.

 

# *IaC Deployment Options*
We’re preparing to deploy Infrastructure as Code for Snowflake and see two approaches:

 

|*Option*|*Pros*|*Cons*|
|*Option 1: Create a new EDP_DEV from scratch; rename existing to EDP_DEV_LEGACY*|* Clean environment aligned with future SIT/UAT/PROD
* Easier to enforce naming and RBAC standards per IaC
* Reduces risk of legacy conflicts|* Requires minor repointing in tactical workflows (e.g. MergeCo)|
|*Option 2: Keep current EDP_DEV and layer new resources*|* No renaming required|* Risk of overwriting existing resources and workflows
* Harder to maintain consistency with SIT/UAT/PROD
* Potential hidden dependencies|

summary: EDP Infrastructure || Repo Configuration - Repo for ALTIDA CI/CD
description: Implement full CI/CD and IaC for the ALTIDA framework in a dedicated isolated Git repository, so that ALTIDA is fully automated (no click-ops), minimally coupled to the core data platform, and can be cleanly removed and replaced in the future without refactoring other repos or shared infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria:
*Repository & Isolation:*

* ALTIDA has its own Git repo containing all ALTIDA code, config, IaC and pipeline definitions.
* No ALTIDA code/config/IaC lives in any core platform or shared infrastructure repo. Other repos can reference ALTIDA only via documented loosely coupled integration points (eg. queues, file locations, APIs).
* Disabling ALTIDA pipelines and archiving the ALTIDA repo does not require code changes in other repos beyond removing those integration references.

*IaC and no Click-Ops:*

* All Snowflake and cloud resources required by ALTIDA are defined and managed only via IaC in ALTIDA repo (no portal or Snowflake UI changes).
* A new environment (eg. DEV/SIT/UAT) can be provisioned from empty to full working ALTIDA by running the documented CI/CD pipeline, with no manual steps.

*CI/CD Configuration:*

* ALTIDA has dedicated CI/CD pipelines in its repo for build, test/validation and deploy to each environment.
* Environment differences are handled via parameters and secrets (eg. Key Vault) not by branching code or hand-editing config in the UI.

*Security & Access:*

* ALTIDA uses its own service accounts and roles (Snowflake, cloud) defined in IaC with least privilege, limited to the layers/resources it needs (Landing/Bronze) and not to curated/core platform components

* The ALTIDA repo includes a short, tested decommission procedure describing how to disable ALTIDA, remove its resources and revoke its identities without impacting the rest of the platform.
* There are no hard dependencies on ALTIDA internals in other repos (no imports of ALTIDA libraries or assumptions about ALTIDA-specific structures). Integration contracts are documented so a future replacement data ingestion solution can plug into the same interfaces.

description:
*Objective*
Investigate and resolve the rounding discrepancy in *Invoice ID: 35358912688554000*, where the total amount in the header ($100.00) does not align with the sum of the line items (approximately $19.00). The tender record also reflects $100.00, suggesting a data integrity or rounding issue between header, line item, and tender tables.

*Steps*

# Confirm with stakeholders whether the total amount should always equal the sum of all line items (excluding rounding tolerances) in the secure database schema.
# Data Engineering team to validate if the discrepancy originates from:
#* Source system calculation or rounding logic, or
#* ETL transformation or aggregation logic in the current data pipeline.
# Identify all affected invoices exhibiting similar discrepancies.
acceptance_criteria:
*Acceptance Criteria*

* *Root Cause Identified:* Source of the discrepancy (source system vs ETL logic) is clearly documented.
* *Fix Implemented:* Data logic corrected and validated so that header totals reconcile with summed line items (within accepted rounding limits).
* *Validation Passed:* QA confirms that post-fix, total header and item-level values are consistent across test invoices.
comments:
AC Nov 4: CW to investigate

AC Nov 18: Total value received by staff from Customer : $100

Mode of Payment: Cash

Line Item Total: $15.98

Rounding: $.02

Total Line Item: $16

Change given to Customer: $84

Invoice Header Amount value and Invoice Line item amount sum may differ whenever there is a cash payment involved. In this invoice:35358912688554000 if someone pays cash as payment and gives $100 to the cashier for products worth $16. Then the Total Amount from the product line item would be $16, and Header Invoice would be $100. It does not take the change returned ($84 ) into account.

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description:
h3. Context

* We need a simple, durable Git repo naming standard for the Enterprise Data Platform (EDP) that works across clouds/regions without future renames. Use lowercase *kebab-case* and avoid embedding env/region/provider in names.

h3. Objective

* Adopt a task-oriented pattern and pair it with CI/CD parameters for multi-cloud/region deployments.
*Naming pattern:* {{edp-<capability>-<task>[-<asset>]}}
Examples: {{edp-infra-provision}}, {{edp-ingest-orchestrate-pipelines}}, {{edp-transform-build-warehouse}}, {{edp-model-publish-semantic}}, {{edp-visualize-publish-dashboards}}. (Lowercase, hyphens only.)

h3. Steps 

# 
# Publish standard and examples in Confluence; notify teams.
# Rename existing repos to the new pattern (no env/region/provider in slug). 
# Update pipelines to use a *matrix* for cloud/region (e.g., {{CLOUD=az|aws}}, {{REGION=au-ae|eu}}).
# Configure Terraform state backends per cloud/region: *azurerm* on Azure, *s3* on AWS. 
# (If using ADF) Deploy from *publish* artifacts/ARM templates, not raw JSON.

h3. Deliverables

* Documented naming standard with examples.
* Renamed repos aligned to {{edp-<capability>-<task>[-<asset>]}}.
* CI/CD updated to matrix by cloud/region; TF backends isolated per target; ADF using publish flow. 

h3. Assumptions - (Optional)

* 

h3.
acceptance_criteria:
* *Given* the standard, *when* repos are reviewed, *then* each name matches {{edp-<capability>-<task>[-<asset>]}} in lowercase kebab-case with no env/region/provider. 
* *Given* multi-cloud/region needs, *when* pipelines run, *then* jobs fan out via *matrix* and deploy successfully per target.
* *Given* Terraform usage, *when* state is initialized, *then* Azure uses *azurerm* and AWS uses *s3* backends with separate keys/workspaces per region/env.
* *Given* ADF deployments, *then* CI consumes *publish* templates/parameters to promote between environments.

** Readers

Below are the scripts

-- 1. Create the IAC service role and data warehouse
USE ROLE SECURITYADMIN;

CREATE WAREHOUSE IF NOT EXISTS INFRA_ADMIN_WH COMMENT = 'WH used for IaC deployments';

GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE WAREHOUSE ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE INTEGRATION ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE ROLE ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE SCHEMA TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;

-- 3. Allow escalation only when approved
GRANT ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE TO ROLE SECURITYADMIN;

-- 4. Create the service account user
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE
 LOGIN_NAME = 'SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE'
 DISPLAY_NAME = 'SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE'
 DEFAULT_ROLE = ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE

 MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD = FALSE

 COMMENT = 'Service account for Snowflake IaC deployments';

GRANT ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE TO USER SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE;

description:
h3. Context

Develop and deploy a CI/CD pipeline for automated build, test, and deployment of Snowflake objects. Manual deployments lead to inconsistent environments and compliance risk.

h3. Objective

* Ensure all database changes and models are deployed automatically through CI/CD pipelines.

h3. Steps 

* Configure Azure DevOps pipelines for Snowflake.
* Add testing steps.
* Use service accounts for non-prod and prod deployments.
* Automate version tagging and rollback.

h3. Deliverables

* YAML pipelines stored in Git repo.
* Environment variable templates for credentials and targets.
* Audit log of deployments.
acceptance_criteria:
* 100% Snowflake deployments through CI/CD (no manual SQL).
* Successful automated test gate before deploy.

*Repository & Isolation:*

* ALTIDA has its own Git repo containing all ALTIDA code, config, IaC and pipeline definitions.
* No ALTIDA code/config/IaC lives in any core platform or shared infrastructure repo. Other repos can reference ALTIDA only via documented loosely coupled integration points (eg. queues, file locations, APIs).
* Disabling ALTIDA pipelines and archiving the ALTIDA repo does not require code changes in other repos beyond removing those integration references.

*IaC and no Click-Ops:*

* All Snowflake and cloud resources required by ALTIDA are defined and managed only via IaC in ALTIDA repo (no portal or Snowflake UI changes).
* A new environment (eg. DEV/SIT/UAT) can be provisioned from empty to full working ALTIDA by running the documented CI/CD pipeline, with no manual steps.

*CI/CD Configuration:*

* ALTIDA has dedicated CI/CD pipelines in its repo for build, test/validation and deploy to each environment.
* Environment differences are handled via parameters and secrets (eg. Key Vault) not by branching code or hand-editing config in the UI.

*Security & Access:*

* ALTIDA uses its own service accounts and roles (Snowflake, cloud) defined in IaC with least privilege, limited to the layers/resources it needs (Landing/Bronze) and not to curated/core platform components
* No shared “god” roles or service accounts exists between ALTIDA and other platform components. Secrets are stored only in approved secret stores, not in code or pipeline definitions.

*Replaceability/Decommissioning:*

* The ALTIDA repo includes a short, tested decommission procedure describing how to disable ALTIDA, remove its resources and revoke its identities without impacting the rest of the platform.
* There are no hard dependencies on ALTIDA internals in other repos (no imports of ALTIDA libraries or assumptions about ALTIDA-specific structures). Integration contracts are documented so a future replacement data ingestion solution can plug into the same interfaces.

acceptance_criteria:

* -Roles and grants created only via IaC.-

* -No changes/deployments made manually-
comments:
* Working on the RBAC documentation:

Added Managed Access Schema strategy to enforce least privilege and enable IaC-driven future grants

*Problem Statement*

Our Snowflake Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) setup, deployed via Azure DevOps, uses a service role ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE to create and manage objects (databases, schemas, RBAC grants) across environments: *DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD*.

However, there’s a challenge:

* Future grants on schemas and objects require either *MANAGE GRANTS* (a high-privilege, organisation-wide permission) or *schema ownership*.
* Granting *MANAGE GRANTS* to the IaC role violates least-privilege principles.
* We need a *fully automated IaC solution* with no manual steps, while maintaining strong access control.

 

*Proposed Solution: Managed Access Schema + Role Ownership Pattern*

* Use *Managed Access Schemas (MAS)* in all environments for consistent IaC behaviour and centralised grant control.
* *Design Summary*:
** Each schema is created as a Managed Access Schema, e.g.
CREATE SCHEMA EDP_${ENV}.SILVER WITH MANAGED ACCESS;
** Schema ownership is assigned to a dedicated role, e.g.
OPS_${ENV}
** The IaC service role (ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE) performs grants and object creation on behalf of the schema-owner role (via USE ROLE or delegated ownership).
** Developers in *DEV* can assume the schema-owner role for flexibility.
** In *SIT/UAT/PROD*, only the IaC pipeline holds this privilege — ensuring RBAC consistency, least privilege, and full automation.

 

*Benefits*

|*Area*|*Outcome*|
|*Security*|No need for MANAGE GRANTS; privileges limited to schema level.|
|*Consistency*|Identical IaC templates across all environments.|
|*Governance*|Centralised privilege control via schema-owner roles.|
|*Automation*|All schema creation and grants handled by IaC pipeline, zero manual steps.|
|*Flexibility*|Developers retain freedom in DEV through delegated roles.|

*In short:*
Standardise on Managed Access Schemas across environments and assign schema ownership to environment-specific roles. The IaC role manages objects and future grants under these roles — delivering *full automation*, *least privilege*, and *end-to-end consistency*.

{noformat}-- 1. Create the IAC service role and data warehouse
USE ROLE SECURITYADMIN;

CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE COMMENT = 'Role used for IaC deployments';
CREATE WAREHOUSE IF NOT EXISTS INFRA_ADMIN_WH COMMENT = 'WH used for IaC deployments';

-- 2. Grant necessary privileges
GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE WAREHOUSE ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE INTEGRATION ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE ROLE ON ACCOUNT TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT CREATE SCHEMA TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;
GRANT MANAGE GRANTS ON DATABASE EDP_DEV TO ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE;

-- 3. Create the service account user
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE
 LOGIN_NAME = 'SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE'
 DISPLAY_NAME = 'SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE'
 DEFAULT_ROLE = ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE
 DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE = 'INFRA_ADMIN_WH'
 MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD = FALSE
 DISABLED = FALSE
 RSA_PUBLIC_KEY = 'MIICIjANBgk..........AwEAAQ=='
 COMMENT = 'Service account for Snowflake IaC deployments';

-- 4. Grant the role to the user
GRANT ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE TO USER SVC_IAC_SNOWFLAKE;

-- 5. Allow escalation only when approved
GRANT ROLE ROLE_INFRA_ADMIN_SNOWFLAKE TO ROLE SECURITYADMIN;{noformat}

description:
h3. Objective

Create and configure Snowflake environments (DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD) using IaC, ensuring consistent configuration, compliance and zero manual intervention. All Snowflake environments must be fully automated via IaC to guarantee consistency, traceability and easy redeployment. No manual configuration.

h3. Steps 

# Design Teraform or scripted templates for Snowflake (accounts, database, roles, warehouse, parameters).
# Define environment variables for DEV, SIT, UAT, PROD (naming, warehouse sizes, privileges)

* Documented best practices and standards for each component.

* Existing documentation is available and up to date for reference.
* Stakeholders are available for review and feedback.

* Documentation is published and communicated to all relevant teams.

acceptance_criteria:
h3. Acceptance criteria

* Document/understand what option is most suitable for MergeCo report

comments:
Have created a Power Automate flow to generate the MergeCo Supply Chain Scorecard.
The flow:

* Extracts the PBI report as a .pdf
* Validates 3 metrics
** Ensures the latest date in the Semantic Model matches the latest date based on a TODAY() date function
** Availability % is between 80% and 100%
** SOH is between $500M and $1B
* Emails the report to distribution list if validation is successful
* Emails a notification alert to the Data Eng team if validation fails

[https://make.powerautomate.com/environments/Default-8bc0280e-b3ad-438a-ba8a-2cf00d19af4a/flows/74c08131-3e07-477c-9442-7a88a2d67751/details|https://make.powerautomate.com/environments/Default-8bc0280e-b3ad-438a-ba8a-2cf00d19af4a/flows/74c08131-3e07-477c-9442-7a88a2d67751/details]

summary: RITM0173487 - Implement Azure DNS Private Resolver - Sprint 10
description:
Currently worked on by Shagun A.

Implement Azure DNS Private Resolver to enable on-premises DNS resolution for existing Snowflake Private Link endpoint ([privatelink.snowflakecomputing.com|http://privatelink.snowflakecomputing.com]).

The Azure Private Link for Snowflake is already configured and operational. This DNS implementation will enable on-premises systems to resolve the private Snowflake endpoint, which is a prerequisite for subsequent firewall access configuration for Enterprise Data Platform and critical applications requiring Snowflake access.

Spoke to Network team and they suggested we create AD security group for snowflake private link access control and add the relevant users who need access to this group as the user laptop ip address is dynamic so this way we can control this via global protect and firewall. 

 

Current status:
acceptance_criteria:
* Azure DNS Private Resolver is deployed and configured
* On-premises DNS resolution is verified
* AD Security Group for Snowflake Access is created
* Firewall and GlobalProtect integration is validated
* Documentation is updated
* -Stakeholder sign-off-

description:
h3. Context

* Connect dbt Cloud to our Snowflake instance on Azure to enable secure, version-controlled data transformations, scheduled jobs, and CI for analytics. The setup will use least-privilege access, correct Azure region selection, and standardized dev/staging/prod environments.

h3. Objective

* Provision Snowflake user/role with least-privilege and a dedicated warehouse.
* Configure dbt Cloud connection: account identifier, Azure region, user/role, warehouse, database, schema; select approved auth (key pair or OAuth/SSO).
* Store credentials in dbt Cloud environment variables; avoid hardcoded secrets.
* Set up dev and deployment environments/jobs; map targets to separate schemas.
* Validate with dbt debug and a sample dbt run; confirm role, warehouse, and permissions.
* Document egress IPs (for allowlisting/PrivateLink), connection details, and handoff steps.

summary: Creating Detailed documentation - Detailed Documentation of work - Sprint 10
description:
h3. Context

* Comprehensive documentation is required to centralise and standardise knowledge on data engineering assets, including ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract metadata, and related sources (e.g., SCAX2012). This will support onboarding, troubleshooting, and ongoing enhancements.

h3. Objective

* Summarise and document the architecture, processes, and metadata for ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract mechanisms, and SCAX2012, consolidating all sources and references in Confluence for easy access and governance.

h3. Steps

# Identify and catalogue all relevant ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract processes, and SCAX2012 assets.
# Gather existing documentation, code, and metadata from source systems and repositories.
# Summarise technical details, dependencies, and integration points for each asset.
# Document best practices, naming conventions, and standards (referencing existing Snowflake and ADF standards).
# Create or update Confluence pages with structured summaries, diagrams, and links to source artifacts.
# Review documentation with stakeholders for completeness and accuracy.
# Publish and communicate the documentation to the engineering and analytics teams.

h3. Deliverables

* Confluence summary pages for ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract metadata, and SCAX2012.
* Linked references to source code, metadata tables, and configuration files.
* Diagrams illustrating architecture and data flows.
* Documented best practices and standards for each component.

h3. Assumptions (Optional)

* All relevant source systems and repositories are accessible.
* Existing documentation is available and up to date for reference.
* Stakeholders are available for review and feedback.
acceptance_criteria:
* All ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract processes, and SCAX2012 assets are documented in Confluence.
* Documentation includes architecture diagrams, metadata summaries, and integration points.
* Best practices and naming conventions are clearly outlined.
* Stakeholder review is completed and feedback incorporated.
* Documentation is published and communicated to all relevant teams.

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description:
h4. *Current State*

* Data ingestion currently relies on a *high watermark strategy*.
* Databases {{pdb19.scax2012}} and {{pdb14.transactionstorage}} are part of an *Always On Availability Group*.
* *Change Tracking* is used but has limitations:
** Cannot be queried from *secondary replicas*.
** Requires *primary replica access*, which we want to avoid.
** Failover introduces *recovery delays* and *manual reconfiguration*.

----

h4. ✅ *Proposed Solution: Implement CDC-Based Ingestion Tool*

CDC is proposed to enable *near real-time data ingestion* with the following benefits:

h5. *Advantages*

* ✅ *Readable from secondary replicas*: CDC change tables are replicated and accessible.
* ✅ *No primary exposure*: Ingestion can run from secondaries.
* ✅ *Full change history*: Captures inserts, updates, deletes with row-level detail.
* ✅ *Supports multiple consumers*: Ideal for sync, audit, and reporting.
* ✅ *Failover resilient*: CDC remains enabled; only SQL Agent jobs may need reconfiguration.

----

h4. ⚠️ *DBA Concerns: Resource Overhead*

CDC introduces overhead due to:

* Transaction log scanning
* Storage for change tables
* SQL Agent job execution

h5. *Mitigation Strategies*

||Concern||Mitigation||
|Log scanning|Enable CDC only on critical tables|
|Storage usage|Tune retention period via {{sp_cdc_change_job}}|
|Job load|Schedule capture/cleanup jobs during off-peak hours|
|Query performance|Index CDC tables if needed|
|Monitoring|Use {{sys.dm_cdc_errors}} and {{sys.dm_cdc_log_scan_sessions}}|

----

h4. 📌 *Next Steps*

* Identify target tables for CDC (minimal scope).
* Review CDC enablement plan with DBA team.
* Confirm SQL Server Agent job configuration and failover handling.
* Design ingestion tool to query CDC tables from secondary replicas.

description:
h3. Context

* Comprehensive documentation is required to centralise and standardise knowledge on data engineering assets, including ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract metadata, and related sources (e.g., SCAX2012). This will support onboarding, troubleshooting, and ongoing enhancements.

h3. Objective

* Summarise and document the architecture, processes, and metadata for ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract mechanisms, and SCAX2012, consolidating all sources and references in Confluence for easy access and governance.

h3. Steps

# Identify and catalogue all relevant ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract processes, and SCAX2012 assets.
# Gather existing documentation, code, and metadata from source systems and repositories.
# Summarise technical details, dependencies, and integration points for each asset.
# Document best practices, naming conventions, and standards (referencing existing Snowflake and ADF standards).
# Create or update Confluence pages with structured summaries, diagrams, and links to source artifacts.
# Review documentation with stakeholders for completeness and accuracy.
# Publish and communicate the documentation to the engineering and analytics teams.

h3. Deliverables

* Confluence summary pages for ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract metadata, and SCAX2012.
* Linked references to source code, metadata tables, and configuration files.
* Diagrams illustrating architecture and data flows.
* Documented best practices and standards for each component.

h3. Assumptions (Optional)

* All relevant source systems and repositories are accessible.
* Existing documentation is available and up to date for reference.
* Stakeholders are available for review and feedback.
acceptance_criteria:
* All ADF pipelines, Snowflake extract processes, and SCAX2012 assets are documented in Confluence.
* Documentation includes architecture diagrams, metadata summaries, and integration points.
* Best practices and naming conventions are clearly outlined.
* Stakeholder review is completed and feedback incorporated.
* Documentation is published and communicated to all relevant teams.

summary: AA - Snowflake Pull Request (Please correct the contents)
description:
h3. Context

* Engineers need to establish and document processes, artifacts, and review steps to ensure Snowflake Pull Requests (PRs) are executed efficiently and consistently.

h3. Objective

* Define and implement a standardised process for creating, reviewing, and merging Snowflake PRs, ensuring code quality, traceability, and compliance with development standards.

h3. Steps

# Review and document current PR workflow for Snowflake repositories.
# Define naming conventions and file structure for PR artifacts (e.g., Flyway script naming, R scripts).
# Create templates and checklists for PR submissions and reviews.
# Implement automated build and deployment pipelines for PR validation.
# Establish review and approval requirements (e.g., peer review, technical lead sign-off).
# Document the process in Confluence and communicate to the engineering team.
# Monitor and refine the process based on feedback and deployment outcomes.

h3. Deliverables

* Documented PR process and workflow for Snowflake code changes.
* PR submission and review templates/checklists.
* Updated build and deployment pipeline configurations.
* Confluence page outlining the process and standards.
* Training or onboarding material for engineers.

h3. Assumptions (Optional)

* All engineers have access to the relevant Snowflake repositories and CI/CD tools.
* Existing code follows baseline Snowflake development standards.
* Required roles and permissions are in place for PR creation and approval.
acceptance_criteria:
* PR process documentation is published and accessible.
* Templates and checklists are available for use in PRs.
* Automated build and deployment steps are integrated with PR workflow.
* At least one successful PR is executed using the new process.
* Feedback from engineers is collected and incorporated into process improvements.

description:
h3. Context

* The ingestion of data from APPRISS and MergeCo Retail is pending completion. These integrations are critical to ensure comprehensive data coverage and enable downstream analytics and reporting.

h3. Objective

* Complete the end-to-end ingestion processes for APPRISS and MergeCo Retail, ensuring data is reliably extracted, transformed, loaded, and validated within the enterprise data platform.

h3. Steps

# Confirm data source access and connectivity for APPRISS and MergeCo Retail.
# Gather and review source data structures, formats, and update frequencies.
# Design and document ingestion pipelines, including extraction, transformation, and loading logic.
# Implement pipelines using standard naming conventions and best practices *1*.
# Populate and maintain extract/load metadata tables for orchestration and monitoring.
# Conduct system, integration, and performance testing of ingestion processes *2* *3*.
# Validate ingested data with business stakeholders and resolve discrepancies.
# Finalise documentation and update Confluence with process details and data dictionaries.
# Transition pipelines to production and monitor initial loads.

h3. Deliverables

* Fully operational ingestion pipelines for APPRISS and MergeCo Retail.
* Updated extract/load metadata and monitoring dashboards.
* Technical documentation and data dictionaries in Confluence.
* Test results and sign-off from stakeholders.

h3. Assumptions (Optional)

* Source systems for APPRISS and MergeCo Retail are accessible and stable.
* Required credentials and permissions are available.
* Business stakeholders are available for validation and sign-off.
acceptance_criteria:
* Data from APPRISS and MergeCo Retail is ingested and available in the enterprise data platform.
* Ingestion pipelines follow established naming conventions and best practices.
* Metadata and monitoring are in place for all new ingestion processes.
* Successful completion of system, integration, and performance testing.
* Documentation is complete and published in Confluence.
* Stakeholder validation and sign-off are obtained.

----

h3. 🔧 *Architecture Overview*

* Snowflake deployed securely on Microsoft Azure using a hub-spoke network model.
* Supports Dev, UAT, and Prod environments with private connectivity and centralised monitoring.
* Designed for scalability, compliance, and high availability.

----

h3. 🛡️ *Security Principles*

* Zero Trust Network: All traffic via private endpoints.
* Network isolation with dedicated VNets and controlled peering.
* TLS 1.2+ encryption for data at rest and in transit.
* Managed identities for secure service-to-service authentication.

----

h3. ⚙️ *High Availability & Governance*

* Geo-redundant storage (RAGRS) across regions.
* Hub-spoke design enables resilient failover.
* Resource tagging, management locks, and Azure Policy for governance.
* Centralised monitoring via Log Analytics at the management group level.

----

h3. 🌐 *Network Architecture*

* Hub subscription connects to Dev, UAT, Prod, and Snowflake via VNet peering.
* Snowflake subscription includes dedicated subnets for endpoints, storage, and VMs.
* Cross-subscription private endpoints enable secure access to Snowflake from all environments.

----

h3. 🗂️ *Subnet & Resource Group Design*

* Subnets allocated for Snowflake, storage, VMs, and future expansion.
* Separate resource groups for application, network, and security components.
* Key Vault integrated for secrets and certificates.

----

h3. 🔄 *Data Flow & Integration*

* Data ingested into environment-specific Data Lakes (Dev/UAT/Prod).
* Processed via Azure Data Factory and Self-hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR).
* Integrated into shared Snowflake warehouse for analytics and reporting.
* Exported to local storage for specific use cases.

----

h3. 🔐 *Network Security Controls*

* NSGs enforce strict traffic rules (allow trusted sources, deny all else).
* Private endpoints for Snowflake, storage, and Key Vault.
* Hub-managed private DNS zones with automatic registration and conditional forwarding.

----

h3. 👤 *Identity & Access Management*

* System- and user-assigned managed identities for secure access.
* RBAC roles assigned for contributors, network admins, and security teams.
* Key Vault access managed via identities and private endpoints.

----

h3. 📦 *Storage Architecture*

* Local Data Lake Storage Gen2 for staging and exports.
* Environment-specific Data Lakes for ingestion and transformation.
* RAGRS replication and private endpoint-only access.
* Managed identities enable cross-subscription access to Snowflake.

----

h3. 📊 *Monitoring & Observability*

* Azure Policy enforces diagnostic settings and Log Analytics across all resources.
* Monitors network flow logs, storage operations, Key Vault access, and Snowflake connectivity.
* Centralised logging reduces complexity and ensures compliance.

project_name: CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution
description: Monitor ExpressRoute throughput utilisation
acceptance_criteria:
# *Metric Visibility:*
#* ExpressRoute connection metrics (e.g., Ingress/Egress throughput) are visible in Azure Monitor or Network Insights.
#* Bandwidth usage can be correlated with ADF pipeline execution timelines.
# *Alerting Rules:*
#* Alerts are configured to trigger when bandwidth usage exceeds a defined threshold (e.g., 70% of provisioned bandwidth).
#* Alerts include pipeline metadata (e.g., pipeline name, run ID) when possible, to trace high-usage executions.
# *Log Collection:*
#* Network bandwidth logs (e.g., from Network Performance Monitor or Azure Network Watcher) are retained for a minimum of 30 days.
#* ADF pipeline run logs include integration runtime IPs or endpoints for cross-reference.
# *Validation Testing:*
#* At least one high-throughput ADF pipeline is executed to validate that bandwidth spikes are captured and logged as expected.
#* Test scenarios simulate concurrent pipeline runs to verify system responsiveness and alert thresholds.
# *Governance & Review:*
#* A monthly review is conducted to assess if bandwidth consumption patterns require scaling up/down of ExpressRoute or ADF optimization.
#* A weekly review to be initially done on until Oct 2025.

ExpressRoute Monitoring - (15 Sep - 29th Sep)

Description
Monitor ExpressRoute throughput utilisation

---

Acceptance Criteria
# *Metric Visibility:*
#* ExpressRoute connection metrics (e.g., Ingress/Egress throughput) are visible in Azure Monitor or Network Insights.
#* Bandwidth usage can be correlated with ADF pipeline execution timelines.
# *Alerting Rules:*
#* Alerts are configured to trigger when bandwidth usage exceeds a defined threshold (e.g., 70% of provisioned bandwidth).
#* Alerts include pipeline metadata (e.g., pipeline name, run ID) when possible, to trace high-usage executions.
# *Log Collection:*
#* Network bandwidth logs (e.g., from Network Performance Monitor or Azure Network Watcher) are retained for a minimum of 30 days.
#* ADF pipeline run logs include integration runtime IPs or endpoints for cross-reference.
# *Validation Testing:*
#* At least one high-throughput ADF pipeline is executed to validate that bandwidth spikes are captured and logged as expected.
#* Test scenarios simulate concurrent pipeline runs to verify system responsiveness and alert thresholds.
# *Governance & Review:*
#* A monthly review is conducted to assess if bandwidth consumption patterns require scaling up/down of ExpressRoute or ADF optimization.
#* A weekly review to be initially done on until Oct 2025.

description: Monitor ExpressRoute throughput utilisation
acceptance_criteria:
# *Metric Visibility:*
#* ExpressRoute connection metrics (e.g., Ingress/Egress throughput) are visible in Azure Monitor or Network Insights.
#* Bandwidth usage can be correlated with ADF pipeline execution timelines.
# *Alerting Rules:*
#* Alerts are configured to trigger when bandwidth usage exceeds a defined threshold (e.g., 70% of provisioned bandwidth).
#* Alerts include pipeline metadata (e.g., pipeline name, run ID) when possible, to trace high-usage executions.
# *Log Collection:*
#* Network bandwidth logs (e.g., from Network Performance Monitor or Azure Network Watcher) are retained for a minimum of 30 days.
#* ADF pipeline run logs include integration runtime IPs or endpoints for cross-reference.
# *Validation Testing:*
#* At least one high-throughput ADF pipeline is executed to validate that bandwidth spikes are captured and logged as expected.
#* Test scenarios simulate concurrent pipeline runs to verify system responsiveness and alert thresholds.
# *Governance & Review:*
#* A monthly review is conducted to assess if bandwidth consumption patterns require scaling up/down of ExpressRoute or ADF optimization.
#* A weekly review to be initially done on until Oct 2025.

summary: Create an SSO approach with SCIM + SAML - part 2
description:
This task involves implementing secure Single Sign-On (SSO) and automated user/group provisioning between *Microsoft Entra ID* and *Snowflake*, using *SAML 2.0* and *SCIM v2*, with all traffic routed through *Azure Private Link* to eliminate public exposure.

The configuration includes:

* Creating and configuring the Snowflake Enterprise App in Entra ID.
* Establishing SAML trust and metadata exchange between Entra ID and Snowflake.
* Enabling SCIM API integration in Snowflake.
* Setting up automatic provisioning in Entra ID.
* Validating SSO and SCIM flows.
* Applying security best practices and ongoing maintenance.
acceptance_criteria:
* The Entra ID Enterprise Application for Snowflake is created and configured with correct SAML attributes.
* SAML metadata is exchanged and validated between Entra ID and Snowflake.
* SCIM API integration is successfully created in Snowflake with OAuth credentials.
* Automatic provisioning is enabled in Entra ID and tested for users and groups.
* SSO login via Entra ID (both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated) is functional.
* All traffic is confirmed to route through Azure Private Link, with no public endpoints.
* Logging and monitoring are enabled in both Snowflake and Entra ID.
* Security controls such as MFA, RBAC, NSGs, and certificate rotation are implemented.
* Documentation and disaster recovery procedures are updated and tested.

h3. Context

* The project requires implementing a CI/CD process for Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipelines as part of the CW Cloud Data Platform Interim Solution. This involves automating deployment steps, ensuring code quality, and enabling smooth release management through pull requests and approvals.

h3. Objective

* To establish and execute a robust CI/CD workflow for ADF, including deployment automation, code review, approval, and scheduling, ensuring reliable and efficient delivery of data platform changes.

h3. Steps

# Complete the deployment checklist for ADF CI/CD.
# Add the necessary trigger(s) to automate the pipeline.
# Create a Pull Request (PR) for the changes.
# Obtain approval and merge the PR.
# Conduct end-to-end testing of the deployment.
# Publish and schedule the pipeline as required.

h3. Deliverables

* A fully operational CI/CD process for ADF, including:
** Documented deployment checklist
** Configured triggers
** Merged and approved PR
** Evidence of successful end-to-end testing
** Published and scheduled ADF pipeline

h3. Assumptions (Optional)

* Required permissions are available for repository and ADF resources.
* Stakeholders are available for timely PR review and approval.
* Test environments are set up and accessible.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Deployment checklist is completed and documented.
* Trigger(s) are added and verified.
* Pull Request is created, reviewed, approved, and merged.
* End-to-end testing is completed with no critical issues.
* Pipeline is published and scheduled as per requirements.

Note - not a daily snapshot - just movement

Going thru logic i.e. filtration.
Will take longer time

Fact_Store_Inventory_snapshot and Fact_Store_Inventory_Intra

ETL Logic onPrem. 

Step 1: 

Insert into Staging : 

{noformat}select rn=row_number() over (partition by DateStampDayOnly, MyCHemID, OriginBranchID order by DateStamp desc, RecordID desc)
 ,*
 ,1 as isPlaceholder
 from Fact_Store_IncrementalSOHChanges
 where DateStamp >= "PreviousDate" and DateStamp < "CurrentDate"
 ) dt2
 where rn = 1 {noformat}

Insert into the new data from source which is only housing data changes 

{noformat}insert Into Staging 
select 
 RecordID, MychemID, AvgRealCost, SOH, DateStamp
 , coalesce(ChangeType, 26) as ChangeType -- set null ChangeType to SOH Import
 , coalesce(SOHChange, 0) as SOHChange
 , StaffID, RealCost, ExpectedSales, OriginBranchID, DateStampDayOnly
 , 0 as SOH_Last
 , 0 as ExpectedSales_Last
 , 0 as LineNumber
 , DateStamp as DateStampOriginal
 , 0 as isPlaceholder
 , hasExcessiveValue
from 
 Store_IncrementalSOHChanges
where 
 DateStamp >= "currentDate" and 
 DateStamp < "nextDate" and
 RecordID > "maxRecordID" {noformat}

Then It Self joins and deletes all records where isPlaceholder = 1 and has a record in the second join where the isPlaceholder = 0

{noformat}delete Staging 
from
(
 select nr.OriginBranchID, nr.MyCHemID
 from Staging nr
 where 
 nr.isPlaceholder = 0
 and nr.DateStamp >= @currentDate
 and nr.DateStamp < @nextDate 

) dt
where 
 Staging.isPlaceholder = 1
 and Staging.DateStamp >= "currentDate"
 and Staging.DateStamp < "nextDate"
 and Staging.OriginBranchID = dt.OriginBranchID
 and Staging.MychemID = dt.MychemID{noformat}

this ensures that we will have one record for every ChemID , for every Store fore everyday. 

The ETL for this table must be really thought through as it can get quite resource hungry.

split this task to part 2 for next sprint - please adjust story point as per req

summary: Provision Data Platform Azure Subscriptions (Non-Prod & Prod) with Env Isolation, RBAC and Network Controls
description:
h2. Title

Provision Azure Subscriptions for Data Platform (Non-Prod + Prod) with Environment Isolation, RBAC, and Network/Firewall Patterns

----

h2. Summary

We are changing the subscription strategy. Instead of separate subscriptions per environment, we will have:

* *1x Non-Prod subscription* containing *DEV, SIT, UAT* (must remain isolated from each other)
* *1x Prod subscription* containing *PROD only* (isolated from Non-Prod)

Please provision and configure both subscriptions following the existing DEV patterns for networking, firewalling, routing, and foundational resources.

----

h2. Scope / Requirements

h3. 1) Subscription Provisioning

Create and configure the following subscriptions:

*A. Non-Prod Subscription*

* Hosts *DEV*, *SIT*, *UAT* in the same subscription *but isolated* (see Isolation section below)
* Provision foundational resources per environment:
** VNets and subnets (per environment)
** Key Vaults (per environment)
** Storage accounts / Blob storage (per environment)
** Any standard baseline resources used in existing DEV setup (log analytics, monitoring, etc. if applicable)

*B. Prod Subscription*

* Hosts *PROD only*
* Provision the same baseline foundational resources as required for PROD:
** VNet/subnets
** Key Vault
** Storage/Blob
** Any standard baseline resources

----

h3. 2) Environment Isolation Requirements

Even though DEV/SIT/UAT live inside the *Non-Prod subscription*, they must be isolated as if they were separate environments.

Minimum isolation requirements:

* Separate VNets per environment (preferred), or strict subnet segmentation with enforced controls
* No lateral traffic between DEV ↔ SIT ↔ UAT unless explicitly approved and implemented via controlled rules
* Resource naming, tags, and RG boundaries must clearly identify environment

*Prod isolation:*

* No network peering or access paths from Non-Prod to Prod unless explicitly approved (and must be documented if required)

----

h3. 3) Access Management (RBAC)

Create Azure AD groups (or align to existing naming standards) for each subscription and environment.

*Non-Prod:*

* Groups for *DEV Contributors / DEV Readers*
* Groups for *SIT Contributors / SIT Readers*
* Groups for *UAT Contributors / UAT Readers*
* Any additional groups required for platform operations (e.g., Network Admins, Key Vault Admins, Security Readers), based on existing standards

Assign appropriate RBAC roles to these groups:

* Subscription / RG / resource-level assignments must align to least privilege
* DEV/SIT/UAT groups should have access only to their environment scope (RGs/resources)

*Prod:*

* Groups for *PROD Contributors / PROD Readers*
* Restricted admin groups as per standard operations model

----

h3. 4) Firewall Configuration

Update firewall rules (Azure + on-prem as needed) to support the new structure.

*Non-Prod (SIT and UAT specifically, DEV already exists as pattern):*

* Allow *SIT and UAT subnets* access to required *on-prem resources*
* Enable outbound access from *SIT and UAT* to the internet where required
* Explicitly allow *Self-hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR)* outbound access for software installation and required runtime operations
* Follow the *existing DEV environment pattern* for these rules (mirror approach and controls)

*Prod:*

* Apply Prod-standard firewall posture (typically tighter than Non-Prod), following existing production patterns

----

h3. 5) Routing & Network Patterns

* Apply the existing routing/firewall patterns used in other environments to maintain consistency
* Ensure both *on-prem* and *Azure firewall* rules/routing are updated accordingly
* Ensure route tables / forced tunneling / egress patterns match the standard architecture used today

----

h2. Deliverables / Definition of Done

* *Non-Prod subscription* created and visible
* *Prod subscription* created and visible
* Non-Prod: DEV/SIT/UAT *isolated* via approved network pattern (documented)
* Foundational resources provisioned per environment (VNet/subnets, KV, Storage, etc.)
* AAD groups created and RBAC assignments completed (per env + per subscription)
* Firewall and routing updated (Azure + on-prem as required), including SHIR outbound needs
* Short handover note / diagram or summary confirming:
** network layout
** group names + RBAC scopes
** firewall/routing changes made

----

h2. Notes / Guidance

* Please *reuse existing DEV patterns* wherever possible (naming, tagging, routing, firewall rule structure, baseline resources).
* If any standard conflicts with the “separate VNets per env” preference, propose the closest compliant isolation approach and document it in the ticket.

----

[+Task 148083+|https://dev.azure.com/MyChemist/Enterprise%20Data%20Platform%20Implementation/_workitems/edit/148083]{{: Create Request for Dev Azure Subscription Creation- REQ0136676 created}}

[+Task 148097+|https://dev.azure.com/MyChemist/Enterprise%20Data%20Platform%20Implementation/_workitems/edit/148097]{{: Create QA Azure Subscription}}

[+Task 148114+|https://dev.azure.com/MyChemist/Enterprise%20Data%20Platform%20Implementation/_workitems/edit/148114]{{: Create Request to Configure Azure Firewall}}
acceptance_criteria:
h3. A. Subscription scope and confirmation

* The *existing DEV subscription* is confirmed and documented as *Non-Prod* (subscription name/ID + management group).
* The *existing PROD subscription* is confirmed and documented as *Prod* (subscription name/ID + management group).
* No new subscriptions are created.

h3. B. Resource group and naming standards

* Separate *Resource Groups per environment* exist in the Non-Prod subscription (minimum):
** DEV RGs clearly labeled as DEV
** SIT RGs clearly labeled as SIT
** UAT RGs clearly labeled as UAT
* All resources created for SIT/UAT include required *environment tags* and naming patterns consistent with existing DEV standards.

h3. C. Environment network isolation (Non-Prod)

* SIT and UAT are provisioned with *separate VNets per environment* (preferred) OR a documented alternative that meets isolation requirements (if standards require shared VNet).
* There is *no direct network peering* between DEV ↔ SIT ↔ UAT VNets (if hub/spoke is used, spokes only peer to the approved hub).
* *Lateral traffic is blocked* between DEV, SIT, and UAT address spaces using the approved controls (NSGs/UDRs/Firewall policy), with deny rules documented.
* Any required exceptions to lateral traffic are:
** explicitly approved,
** implemented via controlled rules,
** and documented in the ticket/handover.

h3. D. Non-Prod ↔ Prod isolation

* There is *no peering, routing path, or access path* from Non-Prod to Prod unless explicitly approved and documented.
* If any approved connectivity is required, the ticket includes:
** justification,
** architecture summary (path),
** and implemented controls (firewall rules, routing, scope).

h3. E. Foundational resources per environment

For *SIT and UAT* in the Non-Prod subscription, the following are provisioned and validated:

* VNet + required subnets (aligned to DEV patterns)
* Key Vault (per environment)
* Storage Account/Blob (per environment)
* Baseline monitoring/logging resources or integrations per DEV standard (e.g., diagnostics to Log Analytics, activity log forwarding), if applicable in your environment

h3. F. RBAC: environment-scoped access (least privilege)

* Entra ID security groups exist (created or confirmed) for:
** DEV Contributors / DEV Readers
** SIT Contributors / SIT Readers
** UAT Contributors / UAT Readers
** PROD Contributors / PROD Readers
* DEV/SIT/UAT contributor/reader groups are scoped to *their own environment RGs/resources only* (no subscription-wide Contributor for env groups).
* Any platform operational groups required by standard (e.g., Network Admins, Security Readers, Key Vault Admins) are created/aligned and assigned per least privilege.

h3. G. PIM: zero standing Owner access

* Dedicated Owner groups exist for:
** SIT Owners
** UAT Owners
** PROD Owners
* Each Owner group is configured in *PIM as Eligible only*, with:
** MFA required
** mandatory business justification
** maximum activation duration *4 hours*
* No user has permanent Owner rights in SIT/UAT/PROD scope (zero standing access).

h3. H. Firewall and routing

* For *SIT and UAT*, firewall rules (Azure + on-prem where required) are implemented following the DEV pattern to:
** allow access to required on-prem resources
** allow outbound internet access where required
** explicitly allow SHIR outbound access for installation and operations
* Routing (UDRs/forced tunneling/egress pattern) matches the approved standard architecture used today (and is documented).

h3. I. Azure DevOps agent connectivity

* Approved Azure DevOps agent pools can connect to required resources (Key Vault/Storage/etc.) in:
** Non-Prod (DEV/SIT/UAT) environments
** Prod subscription
* Any allowlisting/whitelisting is:
** implemented via approved change process,
** documented (source, destination, ports/protocols),
** and aligned to least privilege.

h3. J. Handover documentation

A short handover note (or diagram) is attached to the ticket including:

* Non-Prod network layout (DEV/SIT/UAT) and isolation approach
* Prod isolation confirmation
* List of created RGs and core resources per environment
* Group names and RBAC scopes (what has access to which RG/resource)
* Summary of firewall/routing changes (Azure + on-prem)

h3. I. Azure DevOps agent connectivity

** implemented via approved change process,
** documented (source, destination, ports/protocols),
** and aligned to least privilege.

h3. J. Handover documentation

A short handover note (or diagram) is attached to the ticket including:

* Non-Prod network layout (DEV/SIT/UAT) and isolation approach
* Prod isolation confirmation

* Maintaining encryption and key management
* Keeping recovery and DR runbooks updated

description:
This task involves implementing secure Single Sign-On (SSO) and automated user/group provisioning between *Microsoft Entra ID* and *Snowflake*, using *SAML 2.0* and *SCIM v2*, with all traffic routed through *Azure Private Link* to eliminate public exposure.

The configuration includes:

* Creating and configuring the Snowflake Enterprise App in Entra ID.
* Establishing SAML trust and metadata exchange between Entra ID and Snowflake.
* Enabling SCIM API integration in Snowflake.
* Setting up automatic provisioning in Entra ID.
* Validating SSO and SCIM flows.
* Applying security best practices and ongoing maintenance.
acceptance_criteria:

* SAML metadata is exchanged and validated between Entra ID and Snowflake.

* Automatic provisioning is enabled in Entra ID and tested for users and groups.
* SSO login via Entra ID (both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated) is functional.
* All traffic is confirmed to route through Azure Private Link, with no public endpoints.
* Logging and monitoring are enabled in both Snowflake and Entra ID.
* Security controls such as MFA, RBAC, NSGs, and certificate rotation are implemented.
* Documentation and disaster recovery procedures are updated and tested.

Calculate daily data source sizes

Description
As a DBA, I want to collect the daily sizes of source data tables for TransactionStorage.

---

Acceptance Criteria
Get the data sizes of transactionStorage tables.

* *Data Collection*
** Retrieve the *daily size (in MB/GB)* of each table in the {{TransactionStorage}} schema.
** Include the following tables at minimum:
{{BranchOrderItems}}
{{BranchOrders}}
{{Store_IncrementalSOHChanges}}
{{Transactions}}
{{Transactions_Invoice}}
* *Row Count Metrics*
** Capture the *average number of rows added daily* for each table listed above.
** Use production environment data for accuracy.
* *Output Format*
** Present the data in a *tabular format* with columns:
{{TableName}}
{{AvgDailyRows}}
{{DailySizeMB}}
** Optionally include a timestamp or date for each data point.
* *Automation*
** The data collection process should be *automated to run daily*.
** Results should be stored or logged in a location accessible to the DBA team (e.g., shared folder, dashboard, or monitoring tool).
* *Validation*
** Ensure the script or process runs successfully for at least *3 consecutive days* without errors.
** Validate that the reported sizes and row counts match actual database metrics.

SQL access control error:

{noformat}Insufficient privileges to operate on table 'CUSTINVOICETRANS'{noformat}

@user I am assign to OPS_DEV_RO read only role. Please grant delete permission for this table.

Duplicates removed from the CUSTINVOICETRANS Table.

There is no straight forward delete as this table does not have any unique column to identify the delete and snowflake does not support rownum, cte and qualify for deleting duplicates without unique column. Used the below workaround to achieve this.

Actions Taken: -

* Created CUSTINVOICETRANS_DuplicatesRemoved with distinct records.
* Renamed CUSTINVOICETRANS to CUSTINVOICETRANS_Backup.
* Renamed the new table to CUSTINVOICETRANS.

Fact_Store_Inventory_snapshot and Fact_Store_Inventory_Intra

ETL Logic onPrem. 

Step 1: 

Insert into Staging : 

{noformat}select rn=row_number() over (partition by DateStampDayOnly, MyCHemID, OriginBranchID order by DateStamp desc, RecordID desc)
 ,*
 ,1 as isPlaceholder
 from Fact_Store_IncrementalSOHChanges
 where DateStamp >= "PreviousDate" and DateStamp < "CurrentDate"
 ) dt2
 where rn = 1 {noformat}

Insert into the new data from source which is only housing data changes 

{noformat}insert Into Staging 
select 
 RecordID, MychemID, AvgRealCost, SOH, DateStamp
 , coalesce(ChangeType, 26) as ChangeType -- set null ChangeType to SOH Import
 , coalesce(SOHChange, 0) as SOHChange
 , StaffID, RealCost, ExpectedSales, OriginBranchID, DateStampDayOnly
 , 0 as SOH_Last
 , 0 as ExpectedSales_Last
 , 0 as LineNumber
 , DateStamp as DateStampOriginal
 , 0 as isPlaceholder
 , hasExcessiveValue
from 
 Store_IncrementalSOHChanges
where 
 DateStamp >= "currentDate" and 
 DateStamp < "nextDate" and
 RecordID > "maxRecordID" {noformat}

Then It Self joins and deletes all records where isPlaceholder = 1 and has a record in the second join where the isPlaceholder = 0

{noformat}delete Staging 
from
(
 select nr.OriginBranchID, nr.MyCHemID
 from Staging nr
 where 
 nr.isPlaceholder = 0
 and nr.DateStamp >= @currentDate
 and nr.DateStamp < @nextDate 

) dt
where 
 Staging.isPlaceholder = 1
 and Staging.DateStamp >= "currentDate"
 and Staging.DateStamp < "nextDate"
 and Staging.OriginBranchID = dt.OriginBranchID
 and Staging.MychemID = dt.MychemID{noformat}

this ensures that we will have one record for every ChemID , for every Store fore everyday. 

The ETL for this table must be really thought through as it can get quite resource hungry.
